- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline (e.g., >80 → 70), apply downward correction of 5–10% to prevent overshoot.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–2 days (e.g., model peaks 2 days ahead), adjust forecast to align with 1-day lagged mean of recent 7-day window.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and model is high, apply mean reversion: subtract 2–5% from forecast if price has been above 80 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is >85 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce by 5–10% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), model tends to overreact; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing 3-day moving average.
